newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: MERRILL LYNCH SAYS LITHUANIA CURRENCY FEARS OVER.
newsitem.headline: MERRILL LYNCH SAYS LITHUANIA CURRENCY FEARS OVER.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch says that fears that the Lithuanian government will quickly end the country's currency board have subsided, restoring investor confidence in the Baltic state.
"Since the elections in the fall, the credit and financial story has improved considerably in Lithuania," one Merrill analyst told Reuters by telephone.
"A lot of people were very concerned at first about the government's plans to do away with the currency board," he said.
"But the government seems to be dealing with the currency board now in a manner that makes sense," he added.
The right-of-centre government headed by Gediminas Vagnorius sparked investor concerns in the wake of last fall's elections when it said it would swiftly scrap the currency board.
Under the system, the central bank guarantees that it will keep one dollar in reserve for every four litas in circulation, freezing the exchange rate at that level.
The government has since backed down from its post-election vow and says the system will be gradually scrapped over a two to three year period, starting with repo auctions next month.
The Merrill analyst added that the government's commitment to privatise key assets in the energy sector and other strategic areas was welcome.
"It sounds like the government is going to sell firms that were off limits before, including those in the energy sector, and that it the right move at this stage," he said.
He also said that Lithuania should acquire a good rating from Standard and Poor's, which is expected in the next two or three months ahead of a planned $200 million eurobond.
"Lithuania's S&P rating should be a BB+ or a BBB-," the analyst said.
